Poète grec né à Ioulis, sur l'île de Céo: Greek poet born at Ioulis, on the island of Ceos. He is said to be the first poet to charge for his work. The legend of Scopas's banquet, told by Cicero, makes him the inventor of the art of memory. He died at 90 according to the Parian Marble.
Philosophe athénien, élève de Socrate. I: Athenian philosopher, pupil of Socrates. He founded the Academy around 383 BC. In the Meno, learning is recollecting; in the Phaedrus, writing makes us forget. All his works have come down to us.
Philosophe et homme de cour grec, ami du: Greek philosopher and courtier, friend of King Mithridates VI of Pontus, nicknamed the Roman-hater. Cicero, Quintilian and Pliny praise his memory: he is said to have stored his memories in 360 places of the zodiac.
Théologien d'origine allemande, maître d: Theologian of German origin, master of the school of the abbey of Saint-Victor in Paris. His Didascalicon teaches how to study and sort knowledge; he advises a rigid order, with a well-defined beginning, to remember.
Philosophe et missionnaire majorquin. Ap: Majorcan philosopher and missionary. After visions in 1263, he conceived a universal Art combining principles noted by letters. He wrote in Catalan as well as Latin; Leibniz would draw on him.
Jésuite italien né à Macerata, arrivé à: Italian Jesuit born in Macerata, who reached Macao in 1582. He wrote a memory treatise in Chinese in 1596, drew up a map of the world in Chinese characters in 1602 and translated Euclid with Xu Guangqi. He died in Beijing.
Mathématicien et astronome d'origine bas: Mathematician and astronomer of Basque origin, a teacher in Paris. His Cursus mathematicus (1634-1637) invented notations, including ⊥, and proposed the first known method for turning digits into consonants. A crater on the Moon bears his name.
Journaliste scientifique allemand. En 19: German science journalist. In 1972, in So lernt man lernen, he described his card box: a card answered correctly moves up one compartment, a missed card goes back to the start.
Neuropsychologue soviétique né à Kazan,: Soviet neuropsychologist born in Kazan, often described as the father of modern neuropsychology, a colleague of Vygotsky. He followed the mnemonist Shereshevsky for years and published his case in 1968.
Psychologue né en Estonie, émigré au Can: Psychologist born in Estonia, who emigrated to Canada in 1949. In 1972, he distinguished episodic memory and semantic memory; in 1973, with Donald Thomson, he stated the principle of encoding specificity.
Psychologue américain né à Charleston, l: American psychologist born in Charleston, one of the founders of cognitive psychology. His 1956 article on the number seven is one of the most cited in the discipline. He co-founded a centre for cognitive studies at Harvard in 1960.
Auteur et animateur de télévision, il po: Author and television presenter, he popularised mind maps with the programme and book Use Your Head, in 1974. He founded the World Memory Championship and co-founded the Mind Sports Olympiad.
Neuroscientifique irlandaise née à Dubli: Irish neuroscientist born in Dublin. Her 2000 study showed that the hippocampus of London taxi drivers reshapes itself as they learn the city map. Ig Nobel Prize 2003, Fellow of the Royal Society in 2016.
